title: Bigfoot! at New York City Center #bigfootthemusical #bigfootmusical #...
transcript: Mark my words, every community theatre will be doing the show in the next five to ten years. Bigfoot! is a campy new musical that pleasantly surprised me — not that I expected it to be bad or anything, but I guess I was wondering why this topic necessitates a musical. And while I think that question still remains unanswered, I can't deny that the show was really fun. The story takes place in the run down, economically disadvantaged town of Muddirt, where local residents suffer at the hands of big corporations and corrupt local politicians — I noticed some similarities to Urinetown in this regard. The mayor uses Bigfoot as a distraction from his shady doings, giving the working class a direction to displace their negative energy. But for being painted as a scary outsider, Bigfoot is anything but — he's actually the most eloquent character in the whole show. The material is solid, with the jokes being largely satirical and comedically verbose. Every character is over the top in one way or another, and I liked how the jokes became increasingly ridiculous over the course of the show. Despite this production only featuring six actors, there's a lot of doubling, so it could easily be scaled up, making it a great future contender for schools and community theatres everywhere. If you want to see it now with Broadway-level talent, it's currently running at City Center through April. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: Creator clearly saw the show and provides opinions about the production, story, and quality
